steps.content: [Office]
The reception area was never quiet.
An endless procession flowed through—people reporting crimes, filing complaints, grieving lost belongings, raging about noise violations.
Murphy worked at a desk near the back, an unremarkable station where the legs wobbled, the drawer stuck at the midpoint, and the overhead light blinked sporadically.
A perfect fit for her. At least, that's what her colleagues assumed.

steps.speaker: Colleague
steps.content: Murphy, step away from the terminal for now, alright? Last time you touched it, we got a blue screen for half an hour.

steps.speaker: Colleague
steps.content: And the water cooler... she broke the dispenser button just yesterday.

steps.speaker: Colleague
steps.content: No way, even the water cooler?

steps.speaker: Colleague
steps.content: It's Murphy. You think the name's just for show?
Those words had long since lost their sting.
It wasn't that people genuinely disliked her. Not most of them, anyway. She'd simply caused enough trouble that avoidance had become second nature to everyone around her.
Murphy dropped her gaze, pulling the instant coffee she'd just prepared toward herself.
Then, with impeccable timing, the bottom of the paper cup gave way, and scalding coffee spilled over the desk and streamed onto the floor.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...I'm sorry.

steps.speaker: Colleague
steps.content: See? Told you.

steps.speaker: Colleague
steps.content: It's fine, it's fine. The rag's over there. Don't panic—wait, don't stand up! The floor's wet!
Pop.
The words had barely left her mouth when Murphy stepped squarely into the spill and went crashing backward, chair and all.
The office fell silent for a beat. Then came the stifled laughter, the weary sighs, the pointed indifference of those too accustomed to bother.
Only the colleague by the window rose to her feet.

steps.speaker: Kiki
steps.content: All right, that's enough. It's not like she did it on purpose.

She came over, hauled Murphy to her feet, and shoved her own tissue box into Murphy's hands along the way. The whole thing looked effortless, like she'd done it so many times it was muscle memory now.

steps.speaker: Kiki
steps.content: Did you hurt your knees?

steps.speaker: Kiki
steps.content: Good. Next time, don't fill your cup so full.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...I'm sorry.

steps.speaker: Kiki
steps.content: See? You're doing it again.

steps.speaker: Kiki
steps.content: It's not like I'm blaming you.
Murphy lifted her head and stole a cautious glance at the person before her.

Kiki was one of the few at reception who still spoke to her willingly. It wasn't pity. Kiki simply drew a clean line between misfortune and character: bad luck was bad luck, but a good person was a good person.
Over time, they fell into a rhythm: working shifts side by side, sharing discounted convenience store meals, staring blankly together at the endless paperwork on night shifts.
In Kiki's company, Murphy brightened considerably. Kiki had even bought her a four-leaf clover necklace, a small charm meant to coax better luck her way.
It felt like friendship. At least, it did to Murphy.
[Scene Change]
One perfectly ordinary afternoon, all hell broke loose on Eastside's outskirts. A Sinner riot exploded into chaos, loud and violent.

Orders collided over the comms, dispatches tangled mid-transmission, casualty figures kept climbing with every update. In the operations hall, screen after screen lit up, painting the room in a fever of blinking lights.

steps.speaker: Alarm
steps.content: Emergency mobilization order issued.

steps.speaker: Alarm
steps.content: All able-bodied personnel report to the assembly point immediately and stand by.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...Everyone? That means us too?

steps.speaker: Kiki
steps.content: The Suspect R you're after is hiding out at the SALVA Hospital on the west of the square—that's a well-known Sinner force.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Great. I've only done first aid training twice.
Kiki said it lightly, but her hands were already flying through the supply box. Gauze, tourniquets, portable syringes...
Murphy just stood there, rooted to the spot. She worked at reception, and so did Kiki.
Their whole job was registering names and pushing paper, basically customer service with a badge. And now they were marching into the Mania site with everyone else.
...How did things ever get this bad?

steps.speaker: Kiki
steps.content: Hey. Stop spacing out. Take that white box.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...Oh, okay.

steps.speaker: Kiki
steps.content: Are you scared?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...Yeah.

steps.speaker: Kiki
steps.content: Me too.
But neither of them uttered a single word of complaint.
[Scene Change]
The district had come apart at the seams—smoke, fire, sirens screaming, figures fleeing in every direction, and beyond it all, Mania heaving with those sick, unsettling undulations.
Murphy's thoughts narrowed to a single thread, repeating like a prayer: stop the bleeding first, then dress the wound.
Stop the bleeding, then dress the wound. The words came easily. The work did not.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: D-don't move... Press down here first.

steps.speaker: Injured
steps.content: Gasp...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I'm sorry... No, I mean, just hang on, almost done...
Kiki was just a short distance away, working alongside two other colleagues to guide the wounded behind the temporary cordon.
Everyone was simply pushing forward, throwing whatever scraps of training and instinct they had into the chaos, hoping desperately that nothing else would go wrong.
But fate is rarely so obliging.
Nearby, the door of an overturned transport vehicle suddenly gave way, and half the panel plunged straight downward, directly above the spot where Kiki stood.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Kiki!
Murphy threw herself forward. The panel hit the ground with a brutal clang, its edge raking across Kiki's shoulder and back. Blood bloomed through the tear before the sound even faded.

steps.speaker: Kiki
steps.content: Cough... I'm okay, just grab the box first...

The gauze slipped from her fingers. The tourniquet clasp refused to catch, no matter how many times she fumbled with it. Before Murphy's eyes, the blood kept seeping through, as if it had no intention of ever stopping.
She had never known fear like this. It was not just the terror of watching a life drain away, but the deeper dread of losing her friend.
Later, reinforcements arrived. The Mania outbreak site was temporarily stabilized after higher-ranking Sinners intervened.
Kiki, gravely wounded, survived the treatment. But Murphy became a Sinner.
[Scene Change]

Kiki's wounds took two months to mend. They left a scar, but nothing that hindered her movement. Around the Public Security Bureau, many called it a blessing in disguise, a narrow escape from something far worse.
But Murphy knew the truth. All of it was her fault.

After their night shift ended, the office emptied until only the two of them remained. Murphy stood there clutching her files for a long, weighty moment. In the end, it was Kiki who broke the silence.

steps.speaker: Kiki
steps.content: I know what happened wasn't your fault—
But Murphy shook her head, cutting her off.
Then she reached up and unclasped the four-leaf clover necklace—the one Kiki had given her—and placed it gently back into her friend's hand.
To Murphy, this was the only way she had left to protect her friend.
[Scene Change]
The dim, yellowed old light abruptly dies.
When the maintenance lights flicker back on, you still stand in that corridor on the Bureau's lower level.
Ahead, the black fog has yet to fully disperse in the deeper reaches. And a trail of staggering footprints extends all the way into the darkest depths.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: ...What?

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: Murphy?...
It's Mania. It's broadcasting all her negative emotions outward.
With the Bureau's restoration comes Mania's revelation.
He gestures toward several Apostle phantoms drifting aimlessly in the distance. They appear to have lost BR-005's call, leaving them disoriented and confined to wandering along fading energy traces.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Come on! We're going after her!
